title: Speed to power: the infrastructure solutions shaping the global data centre race
gist: A short Wood Mackenzie teaser for its Q3 2026 Power & Renewables Compass. It argues that new high-voltage transmission, which takes about a decade, is too slow for data centres and compares three faster routes to power: virtual power plants (6-18 months, 19 GW buyer pipeline), grid-enhancing technologies (5-50% more capacity), and around-the-meter projects (24-48 months, but with 3-6 year equipment waits).

insights.claim: 'Speed to power' has become a top priority in the data centre race because new high-voltage transmission takes about a decade to build, far too slow for data centre timelines.
insights.speaker: David Brown
insights.so_what: Solutions that deliver capacity quickly can charge a premium over traditional grid buildout.
insights.quote: New high-voltage transmission is the traditional answer - but decade-long build times are far too slow.
insights.locator: The race to build data center projects

insights.claim: Virtual power plants can be delivered in 6 to 18 months, and data centre buyers are pursuing a 19 GW VPP pipeline led by the US, but new utility and ISO regulations are needed to scale them further.
insights.speaker: David Brown
insights.so_what: This is a growth opportunity for VPP aggregators and distributed battery players, gated by regulation.

insights.claim: Grid-enhancing technologies can unlock 5-50% more capacity from existing transmission lines within weeks to 18 months; Wood Mackenzie offers six policy recommendations to speed adoption.
insights.speaker: David Brown
insights.so_what: Grid-enhancing technology vendors offer cheap, fast capacity, making them a policy-dependent upside play.

insights.claim: Around-the-meter projects that bypass the grid can be delivered in 24-48 months if equipment is already secured and voltage ride-through compliance is confirmed, but in-flight and early-stage projects could face three-to-six-year equipment waits.
insights.speaker: David Brown
insights.so_what: Equipment already secured is a scarce asset, and turbine and switchgear backlogs favour incumbent equipment makers.
insights.quote: But in-flight and early-stage projects could face three-to-six-year equipment wait times.

insights.claim: With US$4.1 billion in new US electrical equipment manufacturing investment announced through 2029, Wood Mackenzie expects supply chain pressure not to ease anytime soon.
insights.speaker: David Brown
insights.so_what: Tight markets for electrical equipment support pricing power for transformer and switchgear makers through the decade.
insights.quote: the pressure on supply chains is not easing anytime soon.
